item.title: Printed Enzyme Ink For Wearable Electronics
item.description: New water-based biofuel cell ink simplifies manufacturing and powers wearable sensors without batteries. A team of researchers in Japan at Tokyo University of Science, has overhauled a longstanding manufacturing hurdle in wearable electronics by creating a printable, water-based enzyme ink for biofuel cells a development that could accelerate the rollout of self-powered wearable health devices. item.title: Electronics Driven Glove Compresses Swelling Upto 25%
item.description: A new soft-robotic wearable uses electronics and shape-memory alloy actuators to reduce hand oedema without clinic visits. Researchers at Cornell University have developed EdemaFlex, an electronics-enabled soft-robotic glove that uses dozens of tiny actuators to relieve hand swelling associated with oedema, with promising results from early home-use trials. item.title: Compact Film Capacitors For Industrial Use
item.description: Compact X2 safety capacitors handle higher voltages and control noise in industrial drives, EV charging systems, energy meters, and other power systems.
